I checked it. That failure was from a stale run, and v0.36.3 is released correctly. Nothing needs fixing.

**What happened:** The `v0.36.3` tag was first pushed on the PR branch's release commit (`a02c41c`), at 00:32. That started the failing run, [43534895833](https://github.com/cv/pit/actions/runs/43534895833). Before the run reached its last step, the tag was deleted so it could go on the rebase-merged commit instead. The step that creates the GitHub release checks that the tag exists, so it stopped with `tag v0.36.3 doesn't exist in the repo cv/pit, aborting due to --verify-tag flag`.

**Current state:**
- PR #369 was rebase-merged at 00:36:21. `main` has both commits separately: `6d7f6d5` (fix) and `f2ddcec` (`chore(release): v0.36.3`).
- The tag `v0.36.3` now points at `f2ddcec` on `main`.
- A second release run for that commit, [43535327850](https://github.com/cv/pit/actions/runs/43535327850), succeeded.
- The [v0.36.3 release](https://github.com/cv/pit/releases/tag/v0.36.3) went public at 00:37:05.
- I ran `release.verifyPublished` with the install check and it passed. The tag is on the right commit and the release has no assets. A fresh clone of the tag installs as version 0.36.3, and a test script ran in the sandbox.

You can ignore the red run or delete it. I didn't change anything, so there's nothing to commit.

To stop this from happening again, release tags should be pushed only after the rebase merge, on the commit that lands on `main`.
